content:
sam: Heads up — GH Actions eval jobs are stuck in "Queued" state on runners 'redwood-eval-1' and 'redwood-eval-2'. PR #842 is blocked.
lia: I saw that on the nightly job around 03:12 UTC. Jobs show 'Queued' for >10m then timeout or never start.
derek: Might be self-hosted runner saturation; runner-manager reported 0 available. Logs show docker pull hanging and a bunch of workflows 'waiting for a runner'.
ci-bot: [autoscaler] scaled up 2 runners at 03:05 UTC, status: provisioning.
sam: Reproduced locally: our workflow defines a matrix with 12 targets, each job pulls a ~3.8GB image and requests 8G memory. Runners concurrency=2 -> huge backlog.
lia: This smells like the containerd/docker pull slowdown + runner concurrency combined. There's a GH Actions bug where containerd lock leads to queue starvation when many pulls start at once.
eva: Quick mitigation: gate PRs on a lightweight smoke job only, and run the full matrix on nightly or explicit dispatch. Avoid blocking merges on long matrix.
sam: Agreed. Also change required status checks: require 'eval-smoke' but not 'eval-matrix' for PR merges.
derek: Long-term: pre-warm images on runner AMIs or switch heavy workloads to Buildkite where we already have an autoscaler for large instances.
lia: Another low-effort fix: reduce matrix fanout for PRs (test subset of models/quant configs) and add a separate 'full-eval' schedule.
sam: Minimal workflow change proposal (smoke for PRs, full matrix on schedule):
```yaml
name: evals
on:
  pull_request:
    paths: ['evals/**']
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 6 * * *'
jobs:
  eval-smoke:
    runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, x64]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: python -m evals.run --suite=smoke
  eval-matrix:
    if: github.event_name == 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        model: [gpt-small, gpt-medium, gpt-large]
    steps:
      - run: python -m evals.run --model ${{ matrix.model }}
```
lia: I'll open the PR to add the smoke job and update required checks.
eva: I'll add a Grafana alert: watch for >2 queued GH workflows for >5m and page on 2+ occurrences in 30m. We can also surface queued time in the eval dashboard.
derek: I'll prototype a pre-warmed AMI with the most common docker images pulled and an updated runner image to avoid repeated pulls. If AMI prep isn't ready, I'll route heavy quantization jobs to Buildkite as a fallback.
sam: Also note: quantization evals keep GPUs busy for long tails — ensure runner labels separate gpu from cpu. We accidentally scheduled small smoke tests on gpu runners this morning which blocked a heavy job.
lia: I'll add a gating rule to prefer 'cpu' label for eval-smoke and reserve 'gpu' label for nightly/full-eval only.
ci-bot: @derek created ticket CI-457: "runner prewarm AMI + autoscale tuning"
derek: Got it, I'll claim CI-457 and try to have a prototype AMI by EOD.
sam: Action items recap: lia -> PR to add eval-smoke + update required checks; derek -> prewarm AMI + reroute heavy jobs to Buildkite if needed; eva -> add queue alert and dashboard metrics; sam -> doc update for contributors on how/when to run full-eval.
lia: One extra note: for PR authors, add a GitHub Action that can run a targeted subset locally via `GHA_RUN_LOCAL=true` to avoid pushing noisy PRs. I'll add a small README snippet.
sam: Thanks everyone. I'll monitor the 06:00 UTC schedule and confirm the smoke gate works.
